newsitem.title: UK: UK APRIL OIL REVENUE DOWN AS OUTPUT SLIPS AGAIN-BANK.
newsitem.headline: UK APRIL OIL REVENUE DOWN AS OUTPUT SLIPS AGAIN-BANK.

text.p: British oil and gas revenues in April tumbled to the lowest level in nine months as crude production slipped for the fifth month in succession, the Royal Bank of Scotland said.
Combined oil and gas revenues in April were down 6.9 percent to 44.5 million stg a day from 47.8 million stg in March, the Bank said in a monthly report.
The loss of revenue resulted from weaker crude oil prices which fell to their lowest point this year in tandem with a seasonal drop in oil output.
Oil revenues were down to 27.3 million stg in April from 30.8 million while gas revenues gained 1.0 percent to 17.2 million.
Oil production fell for the fifth sucessive month by 2.5 percent to 2.51 million barrels per day (bpd) having hit an annual peak in November of last year at 2.708 million. On
year ago figures the there was a rise of 3.3 percent from 2.435 million, the Bank said.
Average monthly benchmark Brent crude fell sharply in April dropping to $17.71 a barrel from $19.17 in March, a drop of 7.6 percent. The sterling price of Brent declined by 8.9 percent against March.
Britain's gas output increased 1.0 percent in April to 9.487 million cubic feet per day after a large fall in March.
Although oil prices have recovered to between $19 and $20 a barrel towards the end of May on the back of speculative trading, prices will come under pressure, the Bank said.

"We expect the underlying over supply - caused by growing non-OPEC output, above quota production in OPEC, and weaker than forecast demand - to place downward pressure on prices in the coming months," said Stephen Boyle, energy economist at The Royal Bank of Scotland.
"Only a failure to renew the UN-Iraq 'food for oil' deal in June or unexpectantly severe OPEC quotas would give grounds for further rises," he said.
